Our compliance lead has a follow-up from the regulator here in Lithuania: they need concrete evidence around log retention and pseudonymization for our Private deployment (VPC) before we publish the integration for internal use. Specifically they want:

- Confirmation that session and debug logs containing customer identifiers (email, account_id) are pseudonymized within 48 hours and fully removed within 7 days unless flagged for an ongoing investigation.
- A mapping to SIG/CAIQ questions that addresses "retention and disposal" controls.
- Proof that customer-managed KMS keys (we will bring our key) are rotated and can be deprovisioned such that data encrypted with retired KEKs cannot be decrypted after a key destruction event.
- A short config snippet or runbook we can hand to our infra team to show how to set TTLs for ephemeral logs in a Private deployment.

Can you provide an evidence pack (artifact list + short technical notes) we can send to the regulator by EOD Friday? If you have a template attestation letter we can sign and include, that would save time.

Hi all — technical details below and attached artifacts. Attaching: eurobank-sig-mapping.xlsx, redwood-config-retention.yaml, audit-proof-sha256.txt (sha256 sums for each exported file).

High-level answers first:
1) Pseudonymization point-in-time:
   - Implementation: incoming PII fields (email, account_id) are replaced at ingestion with a salted HMAC (SHA256) using a per-deployment salt stored in the control plane metadata. The raw PII is only present transiently in memory and is not written to persistent debug logs.
   - Timeline: pseudonymized on ingest (effectively < 1 minute). Remaining debug/session artifacts that may contain original values are subject to TTL-based retention and are deleted by automated purge within the configured window.

2) Retention / deletion specifics:
   - Default ephemeral log TTL for Private is 7d; can be set per-tenant down to 24h or up to 90d via the tenant manifest.
   - Purge workflow: background job enumerates objects with expiry and runs a two-stage delete (soft-delete + final delete after 24h) to allow for quick recoveries. Final delete irreversibly removes objects and updates our internal deletion ledger (note: ledger entries are metadata only and do not contain PII).

3) KMS rotation / deprovision:
   - For customer-managed keys (CMK), Redwood supports wrapping of storage keys under your KEK (you hold the KEK in your KMS). When you rotate or revoke a KEK, new data is encrypted under new wrapping; previously wrapped keys remain unreadable if the KEK is destroyed.
   - If a destruction event occurs, the wrapped DEKs cannot be unwrapped and data is effectively irretrievable. We will include an example policy language for your legal/regulator pack.

4) Artifacts included (see attachments):
   - eurobank-sig-mapping.xlsx — worksheet mapping SIG/CAIQ items to our controls and evidence locations.
   - redwood-config-retention.yaml — example tenant manifest showing TTLs and pseudonymization toggle (see inline snippet below).
   - audit-proof-sha256.txt — SHA256 checksums for export files; includes a redacted purge export showing deletion timestamps.

Inline YAML snippet (from redwood-config-retention.yaml):

---
tenant: eurobank-prod-sandbox
logging:
  ephemeral_logs:
    enabled: true
    default_ttl_days: 7
    min_ttl_days: 1
    max_ttl_days: 90
pseudonymization:
  enabled: true
  algorithm: HMAC-SHA256
  salt_location: control-plane:tenant-metadata
kms:
  key_management: customer_managed
  kek_reference: projects/eurobank-kms/locations/eu/keyRings/eb-keys/cryptoKeys/eb-prod-key
  rotation_policy: "rotate-every-90d"
  destruction_policy: "manual-confirm"
---

Purge example (CLI):
$ redwoodctl purge --tenant eurobank-prod-sandbox --older-than 7d --confirm

Notes on evidence pack: the attached SIG mapping references specific artifacts (export IDs) that we will place in a locked Drive folder. We will provide SHA256 checksums and a short attestation PDF. For regulator sensitivity, we recommend delivery via your SFTP. If you prefer an encrypted Drive share, please provide the destination path and ACL list.

If you want, we can also generate a short sandbox export showing the two-stage delete timeline for a sample session (timestamps: created, soft-delete, final-delete). I can produce that and checksum it by Thursday morning.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Security — Redwood Inference
